Applying for a China visa? Don’t let a simple photo mistake delay your plans. Your visa photo must meet strict guidelines to ensure smooth processing.

The required China visa photo size is 33mm x 48mm, with your face covering 70–80% of the frame. Your head height should be between 28mm and 33mm, properly centered and clearly visible. Make sure the photo is taken within the last 6 months and reflects your current appearance without any edits or filters.

Keep a neutral expression while looking straight at the camera. Avoid smiling, tilting your head, or wearing glasses and non-religious headwear. The background must be plain white, free from shadows, patterns, or any distractions.

Following these China visa photo requirements carefully can help you avoid rejections and ensure a faster, hassle-free visa process.

The team assigned to me did not communicate details to the head and I had to be the messanger of important information between the team members. If the customer has to do this, what is the point of hiring a consultant? I had to keep a check on every single tiny detail about scholarship deadlines, doc requirements. It was as if I was working for them.

I missed the opportunity to apply and get admitted to two of the finest institutions in Europe 'because' of the irresponsibility and incompetency by GO teams members at Dadar.
For ETH Zurich, my consultant 'miscalculated' the CET and IST time difference, thus minsinforming me about the submission deadline. Result: The deadline passed and I could not even submit my application.
For KTH Sweden, my consultant (note : a different person this time) missed noting a document that was required while submitting the application and realized this when it was already too late. KTH told me that I was not admitted to the university specifically because I did not submit that essential document.

If the consultants of a study abroad consultancy miss out such basic things, the most fundamental and obvious things, I don't see how I can give them any credibility.

I missed getting admitted to two universties extremely important for my career and education. It was out of my hands and all we received was a dry apology and no monetary compensation was made.

They may be good with specific UK and Ireland universities, maybe a few in the US (probably the ones that have a high acceptance rate). But if your aim is to apply to some top high ranking universities, I am sorry but Global Opportunities would be the worst choice.

My review is localised to the Dadar branch based on my experience. I hope branches in some other states would be somewhat credible. GO dadar is not.

My recent student visa appointment at VFS Global's German Consulate in Mumbai was a very smooth experience, thanks to a few factors. I had booked a slot for the Premium Lounge, and if you can afford the extra cost, it's absolutely the best choice.
I arrived well before my scheduled appointment time of 12 PM, and because there was very little rush, the entire process was completed much faster than I anticipated. The efficiency of the premium lounge staff was a major factor. The lounge has a dedicated team to guide you through every single step, from document verification to biometrics.
The key benefit of the Premium Lounge is the convenience. If any documents are missing, you can print them right there without leaving the premises. This alone saves a significant amount of stress and time. They also offer services like on-site biometric photo capture, which is incredibly helpful.
While the normal queue can be fast if you're lucky and there's no rush, the premium lounge guarantees a swift and guided experience. And for the little things that make a difference, the lounge offers complimentary tea, coffee, cookies, and a section with sweets and salted chips. While it's impossible to "cover the cost" of the lounge just by eating snacks—as a friend of mine proved by eating 30 chocolates and still barely making a dent—they are a nice touch that adds to the overall convenience and comfort.
One important note for those driving: There is parking available, but it is paid and can be a downside. The cost starts at ₹300 for the first two hours. If you exceed that by even a minute, an additional ₹100 is added, which can quickly add up.
Overall, the VFS Global German Consulate in Mumbai offers a fantastic service. If you're on a tight schedule or just want peace of mind, the premium lounge is a worthwhile investment, just be mindful of the parking fees.

Singapore's primary work visa for skilled professionals is the Employment Pass. It requires a confirmed job offer from a Singapore registered employer. Your employer applies on your behalf through the Ministry of Manpower. There is no job seeker visa or points based entry system that allows you to arrive and search for work.

What Singapore does have is the Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass, launched in 2023. It does not require a job offer but the salary and achievement threshold is genuinely high.
